findings.premise: 'approval-request' is present in TURN_EVENT_KINDS but TurnEvent has NO ApprovalRequestEvent union member yet (S001 reserved the kind only); S004 adds the member.
findings.evidence: stream-events.ts:64-74 TURN_EVENT_KINDS includes 'approval-request' (line 71); comment at :58 states 'S001 sc2 (additive) RESERVES approval-request as a kind S004 fills'. No `interface ApprovalRequestEvent` exists yet. Claim verified.

findings.premise: markerFor has an exhaustiveness never-check (default: const _never: never = event) that a new TurnEvent union member must be handled in.
findings.evidence: markerFor is NOT in stream-events.ts — it is defined in src/chat/markers.ts:43 with the exhaustiveness never-check at markers.ts:76 (`const _never: never = event`), and has a single-sourced webview mirror markerWebviewSource (markers.ts:84) that chat-panel.ts:261 embeds. The LLD's markerFor API entry, the ApprovalRequestEvent dataModel call-sites ('src/chat/stream-events.ts (TurnEvent union + markerFor)'), and migration step 1 ('markerFor null case (stream-events.ts)') all mis-locate markerFor in stream-events.ts and omit that its webview mirror markerWebviewSource must also gain the 'approval-request' case. The never-check requirement itself is correct.
findings.action: During build, edit src/chat/markers.ts for the markerFor 'approval-request'->null case AND update markerWebviewSource (the single-sourced webview mirror) to match; add only the ApprovalRequestEvent union member in stream-events.ts. Treat migration step 1's '(stream-events.ts)' as covering both files (markers.ts markerFor + stream-events.ts union member).

proposedFix.rationale: Correct the file location so the build edits markers.ts (host markerFor + markerWebviewSource mirror), not stream-events.ts, for the exhaustiveness case.

reviewOverride.reason: User approved after reviewing the 1 MED finding (cl2). The MED is a documentation-location correction, not a design defect: markerFor lives in src/chat/markers.ts (with its markerWebviewSource webview mirror), not stream-events.ts. Accepted-with-note — the build will add the 'approval-request'->null case in markers.ts (both markerFor and markerWebviewSource) plus the ApprovalRequestEvent union member in stream-events.ts, and give the new permission-mode control a distinct id/label (#insrc-permmode) per cl11. Design is sound; 10/11 premises verified clean.

qee8aadf4.question: The precise claude stream-json permission control-line schema + codex approval-item schema (field names for requestId/title/detail) are confirmed to EXIST by the 7100435 spike but must be pinned against the installed CLI versions during build; unit tests use scripted samples and the INSRC_LIVE_TESTS suite validates the real shape.
qee8aadf4.rationale: Keeps one internal ApprovalRequest type behind each ProviderMapper (upholds the 'provider difference lives only in the mapper' invariant), survives a cosmetic CLI field rename, and raises a typed parse error on genuinely unknown shapes; paired with fixtures captured from the installed CLIs so the INSRC_LIVE_TESTS suite has a concrete diff target.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: S004 fills sc2's approval event + permission-decision message and adds a CLI permission-mode seam on the adapter spawn, plus an approval-card renderer and the auto-mode status indicator; inline nonce'd CSP (k1), plain replayable transcript (k4), additive contract (k2), CLI flags no REST (k3).

boundary.internal: Consumes sc1 (registers the approval-card renderer) and sc2 (realizes the reserved approval-request event + permission-decision/set-permission-mode messages + PermissionMode). Owns the adapter permission seam: buildArgs permission flags, mapLine permission-request detection, a pending-request registry, and StreamAdapter.decide relaying the decision over the CLI stdio. All via CLI flags/stdio (k3), no REST.

Shell chrome over stable element ids incl. the status bar + edit-mode select.
Concrete message/widget renderers registered into sc1.

nonFunctional.security: Inline nonce'd CSP; textContent/className only; decisions over local stdio+flags, no REST (k3).

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: The turn request, now carrying an optional permissionMode the mapper reads to choose permission flags.

parameters.name: line

parameters.name: turnId
parameters.purpose: Correlates emitted events to the active turn.

api.name: StreamAdapter.decide
api.signature: decide(turnId: string, requestId: string, decision: 'approve' | 'deny'): void

parameters.name: turnId
parameters.purpose: Live turn whose CLI process receives the decision.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.purpose: The permission request being answered (correlation key).

returns.meaning: Looks up the live pending entry; if present, formats+writes the provider control response via write() and clears it; absent/stale => no-op.

postconditions: At most one control response per requestId.
Pending requests auto-cleaned on cancel()/exit — no dangling card.

errorCases.scenario: A permission-decision message arrives for a requestId that has no live pending entry (turn ended, process exited, or already answered/duplicate click).
errorCases.detection: StreamAdapter.decide looks up (turnId,requestId) in the pending-request registry and finds no entry (or one already resolved).
errorCases.response: No-op: nothing written to CLI stdin; the stale decision is dropped at the seam. Optionally warn-logged.
errorCases.userImpact: None — a double-click or late click cannot corrupt CLI state.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI process for a turn exits or is cancelled while permission requests are still outstanding.
errorCases.detection: The run() loop observes proc.exit resolving / cancel() with non-empty pending entries for that turn.
errorCases.response: Auto-clean the pending registry, reset any live card, post the terminal done/error (S002 stop-reset hygiene).
errorCases.userImpact: No dangling unanswerable card after the turn ends; chat returns to idle.

errorCases.scenario: A permission control line is malformed or missing the requestId needed to correlate a later decision.
errorCases.detection: The mapper's permission-request branch parses the line and finds no usable requestId (parse fails or field absent).
errorCases.response: Unparseable line throws (as today); a parseable-but-idless line yields [] (no card).

errorCases.scenario: review mode active but the process cannot accept a decision write (write() undefined, or stdin closed).
errorCases.detection: decide() checks for proc.write before calling; a closed-stdin write throws, caught around the write.
errorCases.response: Skip/absorb + warn; clear the pending entry so the card is not left live.
errorCases.userImpact: Rare misconfig: decision undeliverable but UI does not hang; turn can still terminate.

edgeCases.input: Multiple permission requests in one turn.
edgeCases.expected: Each registered under its own requestId + own card; answered in any order without confusion.
Status-bar updates immediately; the change applies to the NEXT turn's buildArgs, not the in-flight spawn.

migration.stateBefore: run() spawns with fixed per-provider buildArgs (no permission flags); SpawnedProcess has no write channel so a permission prompt is effectively silently blocked; TurnEvent has no approval member ('approval-request' reserved in TURN_EVENT_KINDS only); protocol.ts has no permission-decision/set-permission-mode; render-registry.ts reserves RowKind 'approval' with no renderer; chat-panel .statusbar has '✓ idle' + edit-mode select only. (cli-adapter.ts:35-53/63-76/141/204-207/278-297; stream-events.ts; protocol.ts; render-registry.ts; chat-panel.ts)
migration.stateAfter: buildArgs reads permissionMode (review/auto flags; undefined=today); mapLine emits ApprovalRequestEvent + adapter registers pending entries; SpawnedProcess.write + StreamAdapter.decide relay decisions with cleanup on cancel/exit; markerFor null for approval-request; protocol gains the two messages + PermissionMode; render-registry registers the approval renderer; chat-panel routes the live event, posts decisions, and gains an auto/review status-bar control. Nothing new persisted (k4).

migrationSteps.action: Add PermissionMode + ApprovalRequestEvent union member + markerFor null case (stream-events.ts). Additive.
Add permission-decision + set-permission-mode to WebviewToHost + WEBVIEW_TO_HOST_TYPES (protocol.ts). Additive.
Add optional write?() to SpawnedProcess + wire production SpawnFn; extend fake spawner to record writes + script permission lines.
Add optional permissionMode to TurnRequest; buildArgs appends review/auto flags; undefined => today's argv.
Extend mapLine with a permission-request branch emitting ApprovalRequestEvent + add the pending-request registry (register on emit; decide resolves+writes; auto-clean on cancel/exit).
Register the inline icon-only 'approval' renderer in render-registry.ts webview source (className/textContent, nonce'd).

In chat-panel.ts route the live approval-request to the renderer + wire buttons to post permission-decision; add the .statusbar auto/review control posting set-permission-mode + a mode seg; add handleMessage cases (permission-decision->decide; set-permission-mode->store per-session, apply next turn).
Extend the five chat suites; run full chat suite + tsc locally to confirm green.

migration.backwardCompat: All changes additive. TurnRequest.permissionMode + SpawnedProcess.write are OPTIONAL (exactOptionalPropertyTypes-safe): existing callers/spawners omitting them compile and behave as today; buildArgs undefined => byte-identical argv. ApprovalRequestEvent is a new union member (kind already whitelisted); existing kinds unchanged; markerFor stays exhaustive. Two new protocol messages are additive union members. StreamAdapter.decide is a new method; existing consumers unaffected. ~211 existing chat tests stay green (k2).

alternativesConsidered.name: Fire-and-forget write seam + StreamAdapter.decide()
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add an additive optional write() to SpawnedProcess and a StreamAdapter.decide(turnId,requestId,decision) that formats the provider control line and writes it to the running CLI's stdin.
alternativesConsidered.approach: SpawnedProcess gains an ADDITIVE optional write(). StreamAdapter.decide formats+writes the native control response; mapLine emits ApprovalRequestEvent; the run-loop keeps streaming; buildArgs reads permissionMode. requestId is the sole correlation key with no adapter-side pending state.
pros: Provider difference stays in each ProviderMapper.
cons: No adapter-side guard for stale/unknown requestId.
Correlation invariant enforced only in the webview UI.

alternativesConsidered.name: Awaited pending-request registry inside the adapter
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The adapter holds a Map<requestId, resolver>; on a permission line it emits the event and parks that request until decide() resolves, then writes the native response.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same sc2 shapes + additive write() as a1, but the adapter registers a pending entry per requestId; decide() looks it up, writes the response, resolves+clears; unknown/stale ids dropped; entries cleaned on cancel/exit.
pros: Natural place to auto-deny/clean up on cancel/exit.
cons: More adapter-side state + lifecycle to test.
Leak/deadlock risk if teardown is missed.

alternativesConsidered.name: No live channel — decision folded into a re-spawn via resume/flags
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid any stdin write seam: on a permission request, cancel and re-spawn the turn with the decision expressed as allow/deny CLI flags.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep SpawnedProcess unchanged; on a permission line emit the event, then kill()+re-spawn via resume with the decision folded into --allowed-tools/--disallowed-tools. buildArgs still carries permissionMode for auto.
pros: Reuses kill()+resume; auto is pure flags.
cons: Fights the verified claude host-answered protocol (fails ac2).
Re-spawning discards streamed context; poor UX.
Tool-level allow/deny is too coarse for a single invocation.
Effectively unbuildable against the real CLI.

openQuestions: The precise claude stream-json permission control-line schema + codex approval-item schema (field names for requestId/title/detail) are confirmed to EXIST by the 7100435 spike but must be pinned against the installed CLI versions during build; unit tests use scripted samples and the INSRC_LIVE_TESTS suite validates the real shape.

Whether scope:'session' auto-answer is wired in this Story or deferred: the a2 registry supports it, but ac1-ac3 only require per-request approve/deny — recommend building the 'once' path and leaving 'session' as an optional field the registry can honour later.
